title: 403-429 signal sifting journal
content:
Purpose / context:
- Personal scratchpad collecting repros, snippets, and quick hypotheses for the recent 403 / 429 cluster of incidents hitting hosted-api routes between 2024-11-04 and 2024-11-09.
- This is NOT a formal postmortem; it's a living debug log intended to capture commands tried, weird responses, and next steps before I dump into JIRA.

Observed pattern summary (high-level):
- Two main symptom buckets: outright 403 responses on some authenticated calls, and intermittent 429s on others.
- 403s tend to correlate with calls that include an API key in Authorization header but are routed through specific edge nodes (eu-west-1a and us-east-1c).
- 429s show up across many routes but spike during small bursts (10-100 QPS for a few seconds). 429s sometimes follow after a 200 for the same key (i.e., sudden throttling mid-session).
- Client-side retries (no jitter) amplify the bursts.

Commands / quick repros I ran locally:
1) Basic sanity curl (valid key returns 200):
- curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOD_KEY" "https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
- Response: 200 / content returned. x-request-id: rwd-req-7df2

2) Repro 403 on suspected edge node (force SNI to eu-west-1a using /etc/hosts mapping):
- echo "3.121.45.12 api.redwood.test" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts  # ip for eu-west-1a (test mapping)
- curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOD_KEY" "https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
- Response: 403 Forbidden
- Body (truncated): {"error":"access_denied","message":"key not authorized for region"}
- Headers: x-edge-node: eu-west-1a, x-rate-limit: 1000, x-rate-remaining: 999

Note: x-rate-remaining looks fine -> suggests not conventional rate-limit block. Error text references region authorization. Could be a policy mismatch between auth service and edge ACLs.

3) Rapid burst to reproduce 429 (simple loop from a laptop):
- for i in {1..60}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $BURST_KEY" "https://api.redwood.test/v1/embeddings" -d '{"input":"a"}' >/dev/null & done; wait
- Observed: ~12% of requests returned 429. Response header sometimes included Retry-After: 1
- Example response: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"per-key soft-quota exceeded"}

4) Test with different keys from same org (same org_id, different key IDs):
- key A: returns 200 mostly; key B: hits 429 more often; both created in same org on 2024-09-02.
- Hypothesis: quotas stored per-key in cache that got stale after a backend migration, causing some key entries to have wrong limits.

Logs and snippets (from edge/authed-proxy logs) - sanitized:
- 2024-11-06T14:07:12Z INFO request id=rwd-req-9a2f user=org-218 key=key-b edge=us-east-1c route=/v1/generate status=403 reason=policy-mismatch authsvc_err=403_authorized_regions
- 2024-11-06T14:07:13Z WARN key=key-b burst=20 recent_qps=18 throttle=soft_quota_active -> returned 429 to client
- 2024-11-06T14:07:13Z DEBUG cache miss for key=key-b -> fetching quota from auth-db (latency 80ms)
- 2024-11-06T14:07:14Z INFO cache populated key=key-b quota=1000

Weirdness / contradictions:
- Some nodes return 403 mentioning region authorization while the central auth-db shows the key is allowed everywhere. Means there might be a cached policy at the edge that didn't get invalidated.
- In some 403 responses the x-rate-* headers show remaining tokens > 0. So 403 is not a direct rate-limit signal.
- 429 responses often include Retry-After but not x-request-id; makes correlating to logs harder.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Edge policy cache invalidation bug: after a config change (2024-11-03), edge ACLs kept an older policy that denies some keys in particular availability zones. Cache TTL longer than expected or missing invalidation hook. Explains 403 with region message.
2) Partial rollout of new per-org quota logic: some edges are using per-key counters, others per-org counters leading to inconsistent 429 behavior depending on routing.
3) CDN or WAF layer (in front of edge) is misclassifying some patterns and returning 403 — especially for requests with certain UA or missing X-Forwarded-For.
4) Client retry storm with zero jitter interacts with small per-key burst window and results in short-lived 429s.

Quick experiments to test hypotheses (notes/results):
- Force re-cache: evicted key-b from edge cache via admin endpoint /admin/cache/evict?key=key-b -> subsequent calls from same edge returned 200. Strong evidence for hypothesis #1.
- Route traffic through different POPs using SNI mapping -> different behavior per-pop (403 vs 200), consistent with stale policy per edge.
- Created a synthetic load test with backoff (random jitter 100-300ms) vs no backoff: no-backoff increased 429s by ~3x. So client retry pattern matters but doesn't explain 403s.

Immediate mitigation ideas (fast):
- Fix: run targeted cache eviction across edge fleet for keys created/updated between 2024-10-30 and 2024-11-05. Use rolling script via ops. (PRIORITY)
- Short-term fail-open: make edge policy fallback to central auth if cache shows mismatch and central says allowed (risk: small window of inconsistency).
- Increase Retry-After and add jitter recommendation to SDKs / client docs.

Longer-term considerations:
- Add versioning + last_updated timestamp to key policies and include that in cache entries; use stale-if-error TTL so edges can detect and refresh on mismatch.
- Consolidate quota model to single canonical place (avoid per-key vs per-org split across nodes).
- Improve observability: ensure x-request-id always present on 429 and 403 responses, and return a minimal error-code that maps to our logs for easier correlation.

Next concrete steps for me:
1) Draft short ops runbook to evict caches for affected key batch + validate (how to identify keys: created_at window).
2) Add quick script to run cross-pop curl checks and gather x-edge-node, x-request-id, x-rate-* headers for a list of keys.
3) Blocker check with infra: did any deployment touch edge-policy service on 2024-11-03? Pinged @Marcus.
4) Add JIRA ticket with findings (JIRA-OPS-712) linking the logs above and attach this scratchpad.

Notes-to-self (messy):
- When reproducing locally, be careful: my laptop's ISP NAT leads to similar IP -> edge sticky routing; rerun multiple times to confirm.
- Keep a copy of failing curl commands with --trace-ascii so we can share raw tcp dump if infra asks.
- Remember to test after cache-evict; make sure we still see quota headers.

End of current notes. Will refine into a concise runbook once we confirm cache eviction works cluster-wide.
